pred:
Hi, this is Dana Whitfield, I'm calling about my son Eli's bike situation, and I'm sending this as an email too so it's in writing.

Eli is in Mrs. Okafor's third grade class at Maple Hollow Elementary. I wanted to give you the full picture so nobody is caught off guard tomorrow morning.

Here's what happened.

On Thursday, March 14th, Eli rode his bike to school for the first time since the weather turned warm. He locked it up in the rack by the east gate, the one next to the portable classrooms, around 8:10. When he came out at 3:15 the front wheel was bent almost into a figure eight, and the brake cable had been yanked loose from the lever. He came home pretty upset, and honestly I was too, because that bike is the one we saved up for last summer.

I called the front office the next morning, March 15th, and spoke with Ms. Reyes. She was really kind about it and said she'd make a note and ask the custodial staff to check the rack area. I appreciated that, but I haven't heard anything since, and I know those notes can get lost in a busy week. So I'm following up now, and **I'd really like to know whether anyone saw anything or whether there's a camera that covers that gate.**

I'm not trying to point fingers at anyone.

I know kids are kids, and I know the rack is pretty exposed. What I'd love is a few concrete things. **Could someone let me know whether there are any witnesses, or whether another student has reported something similar.** **I'd like to know if the school has any plan for securing bikes, like moving the rack closer to the main doors or adding a cable lock requirement.** And **if there's a process for a damage claim or a reimbursement through the school's insurance, I'd like to understand what that looks like, even if the answer is that it doesn't apply.**

In the meantime, I've already taken the bike to Ridgeline Cycle on Fulton Avenue. The mechanic, Marcus, looked at it on Friday and estimated about two hundred and forty dollars to replace the front wheel, true the frame, and replace the brake cable and housing. He can have it ready by next Wednesday, March 27th, if we approve the work. I'm happy to send you the itemized estimate if that helps with any paperwork.

Eli is doing okay, honestly.

He's been asking a lot of questions about whether it was his fault for not locking the bike better, and I want to make sure he hears from someone at school that it wasn't. If Mrs. Okafor has a minute this week, I'd love for her to check in with him. He really looks up to her.

**Could you reply to this email or call me at 555-0148 when you get a chance?** Mornings are usually easiest, between seven and eight thirty, since I'm getting the kids out the door. I really appreciate your help with this, and I'm sorry to add one more thing to an already full week for you.

Thanks so much,

Dana Whitfield

Hi, this is Margaret Ellison calling about a message I want to leave for Dr. Patel's office.

Actually, I'm going to dictate this as an email, so please forward it to whoever handles the patient records. It's not urgent, but I wanted to get it down before I forget.

**I'm writing about my appointment on March 14th with Dr. Patel for my knee.** During that visit I mentioned that my son, Daniel, had taken a lot of photos of my recovery progress on his phone, and he'd offered to help me set up a backup so they don't get lost. Your nurse, Carla, was really kind and said I could send over a few of the X-ray images from the clinic portal, so I'd like to know the best way to download them.

I've been thinking about a backup strategy for everything, honestly.

My plan is to keep one copy on an external hard drive that stays at home, and a second copy in a cloud account that Daniel will set up for me on the 22nd. I also want a printed copy of the two most important X-rays, just in case.

**Could you let me know whether the portal allows a direct download, or if I need to request a CD?** My email address is margaret.ellison72@example.com, and my date of birth is June 9th, 1951, if you need it to verify my identity.

Thanks so much for your help, and I hope everyone is doing well over there.

I'll look for your reply by the end of next week.

Warmly,

Margaret

Hi all, it's Dana.

Quick one. The Riverside Community Garden Club is switching over to the new sign-up app for the spring season. Starting March 3rd. Old paper sheet at the shed is retired after that.

Here's what changes.

You'll get a text invite from Priya Venkataraman, our volunteer coordinator, by end of day Thursday. Tap the link, make an account, done. Takes maybe two minutes. Works on phone or laptop.

**The app's called GreenShift.**

It lets you pick shifts, swap with someone, and log hours. Hours matter because the county grant counts them. So log every shift, even the short ones. Last year we lost about forty hours because people forgot. Don't be that person.

Voice feature.

Some of you asked about this. You can dictate a sign-up or a hours log instead of typing. Just press the mic icon and speak. It transcribes and asks you to confirm. Confirm before you leave the screen. Priya tested it with Mr. Okafor on Tuesday and it got "tomato seedlings" right but wrote "Tuesday the fourteenth" as "Tuesday the forty." So check it.

Training.

Two sessions. Saturday February 22nd at 10 a.m., and Wednesday February 26th at 6:30 p.m. Both in the community room at the library on Elm. Bring your phone. Bring your questions. Coffee's on me.

**If you can't make either, email me at dana@riversidegarden.org** and I'll walk you through it one-on-one.

Thanks, everyone.

See you in the dirt.

Dana Whitfield Riverside Community Garden Club

Hi Marcus, it's Dana Whitfield calling about the Harbourside Hall booking for the Fenwick Retirement Gala on Saturday the 14th of June.

I'm dictating this in the car so bear with me if it sounds a bit scattered.

Anyway, **the reason I'm ringing is the power cut on Thursday afternoon.** Our caterer, Ravi from Coriander and Co, said the kitchen lights went out around half past three and the ovens were off for almost two hours, which is a nightmare when you're trying to get forty trays of samosas ready. He had to reheat everything on the portable gas rings in the loading bay, and honestly I think that's why the chicken came out a bit dry.

Oh, and that reminds me, **did you ever get the new extension lead quotes sorted? Never mind, that's a different conversation.** Back to the point.

**What I need to know is whether the hall's backup generator kicked in,** because nobody from your team came over to let us know what was happening, and we were left standing in the dark for about twenty minutes before anyone answered the phone. **Could you check the incident log for Thursday and send me a copy?** I'd also like to know whether the outage was on your side or the network's, because the guests are going to ask me, and I'd rather have a straight answer than guess.

Given all of that, **I'd like to talk about some kind of partial refund on the kitchen hire, maybe ten percent**, since we paid for a fully working kitchen and didn't get one on the day. **Can you give me a call back on 0207 555 0192 this week?**

Thanks, Marcus.

Speak soon.

Hi everyone, it's Maya again.

Quick one, and sorry for the long gap since the last update.

So, the issue with the noise from number fourteen.

Some of you have asked, and a few of you have been on the receiving end of it at the community garden, so here's where things stand. Since March, the house at 14 Alder Lane has had a workshop going in the back garage, and it's mostly power tools, usually between eight and ten on weekday evenings and sometimes all day Saturday. Angle grinder, circular saw, a planer. Not every night. But often enough.

Okay, what we've done so far.

Ruth Okafor, our treasurer, has the log. She started it on the fourth of April and it now runs to thirty-one entries, each with date, start time, end time, and what she could hear. Dev Patel went round on the eleventh of April and spoke to the owner, a man called Gerald Whitcombe. Gerald was polite. He said he'd keep it to daytime. He did, for about a week.

Then on the twenty-second of April we wrote to the council's environmental health team with the log attached. Reference is EH-4471. They acknowledged it the next day. Nothing since, which is frustrating, but Ruth rang them on the second of May and got a case officer, Priya Sandhu, who said she'd visit. She has not visited yet as far as we know.

So **what do I need from you.**

Three things.

**First, if you're affected, keep logging.**

Same format. Date, time, what you heard. **Send it to Ruth directly, not to the group chat**, because the group chat gets messy and she needs clean records.

**Second, don't confront him yourself.**

I know it's tempting. Dev did it once and it was fine, but I'd rather we went through the proper route now. If he comes to you, be pleasant and point him to me.

**Third, if you have photos or a recording of the noise at peak, send those to me, not Ruth.** I'm keeping the evidence file separate.

Meeting.

We're doing a short check-in on Thursday the fifteenth of May, seven thirty, in the back room at the library on Crown Street. Twenty minutes, no more. If you can't come, just reply with a line and I'll pass it on.

I know this isn't the nicest topic.

But the council are supposed to act on this kind of thing within six weeks, and we're at about five now, so it's worth pushing while it still counts.

Thanks, all.

Speak soon.

Maya

Hi Priya, this is Daniel Okafor from Brightline Studio, calling about the laptop order we discussed last week.

**I've settled on the configuration, so I wanted to get it to you in writing before we place anything.**

We're going with the Halvorsen ProBook 14, the 32 gigabyte memory version with the 1 terabyte solid state drive. **We need twelve units in total, for the design team, and I'd like them in the silver finish if that's still available.** If silver is out, graphite is fine.

On the warranty, I'd like the three year on-site option rather than the standard one year. Our last batch had two failures in the first eight months, and the downtime was painful, so I'd rather pay the difference now.

For delivery, the target date is Thursday the 14th of March.

Our office is at Unit 6, Carrow Road Industrial Estate, and someone will be there from eight in the morning to receive the boxes. **If the 14th isn't possible, let me know the earliest date you can commit to and we'll adjust the rollout around it.**

**Could you send me a revised quote with those details, along with the invoice terms?** I'm happy to approve it once I've seen the figures. My direct line is 01603 555 0142 if it's easier to talk it through.

Thanks, Priya.

Speak soon.
